title: ProxyCreate request body
description: Edge's ProxyCreate request schema (openapi.yaml components.schemas.ProxyCreate), generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3) with every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. Admission rules that exist only in Edge's Rust code are not in this schema; resource-schemas/README.md lists them. This is Edge's own API schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md).

AuthMode.description:
`single` — auth plugins run in priority order until the first success.
For `basic_auth` and the Bearer-token mechanisms `jwt_auth`, `jwks_auth`,
and `oauth2_introspection`, a foreign `Authorization` scheme is skipped;
other mechanisms are not covered by this guarantee. Any rejection
returned by a plugin is terminal.
`multi` — auth plugins run sequentially until one succeeds. If none
succeeds, a server rejection takes precedence over the last ordinary
rejection.
In either mode a `401` from the authentication phase carries a
`WWW-Authenticate` field listing every challenge each rejecting
mechanism carried in chain order and then every other applicable auth
plugin's advertised challenge in priority order, merging only
equivalent challenges (same scheme and parameters), falling back to the
generic `ferrum-edge` challenge.

BackendScheme.description:
Wire-level scheme a proxy uses to talk to its backend.

**HTTP family** (`http`, `https`) covers HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3,
gRPC, and WebSocket. Which of those is actually spoken is
determined per-request (content-type, Upgrade/Connection headers,
HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT) — it is **never pinned in config**.
A single `https` proxy transparently serves a mix of REST, gRPC,
and WebSocket traffic on the same backend pool. Backend HTTP/3 is
selected automatically for plain HTTP traffic when the concrete
backend target is classified as H3-capable.

**Stream family** (`tcp`, `tcps`, `udp`, `dtls`) are raw L4
proxies selected by `listen_port`. `tcps` follows the
`http`/`https`, `ws`/`wss` convention (previously spelled
`tcp_tls`). `dtls` encrypts UDP datagrams to the backend using
DTLS 1.2/1.3 (ECDSA P-256/P-384 keys only, version
auto-negotiated).

**Legacy note**: In earlier releases this was the 11-variant
`BackendProtocol` enum including `ws`/`wss`/`grpc`/`grpcs`/`h3`
plus `tcp_tls`. These are no longer accepted on the admin API —
use `backend_scheme` instead.

delay_ms.description: Fixed delay between retries in milliseconds

base_ms.description: Base delay in milliseconds (doubled each attempt)

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failures to trip the circuit open

success_threshold.description: Consecutive successes in half-open to close the circuit

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in open state before transitioning to half-open. `cooldown_seconds` is accepted as an input alias on Admin API, file config, database rows, and batch/restore payloads, and is never returned.

cooldown_seconds.description: Input alias for `timeout_seconds`, accepted on Admin API, file config, database rows, and batch/restore payloads. Never returned: responses always carry `timeout_seconds`. Supplying both spellings in one object is rejected as a duplicate field.

failure_status_codes.description: HTTP status codes that count as failures

half_open_max_requests.description: Maximum concurrent probe requests allowed in half-open state

trip_on_connection_errors.description: Whether connection-level errors (TCP refused, DNS failure, TLS handshake error, connect timeout) count as circuit breaker failures independently of failure_status_codes. When true (default), connection errors always trip the breaker. When false, only real HTTP response status codes in failure_status_codes are counted.

plugin_config_id.description: ID of the PluginConfig to apply to this proxy

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID auto-generated if omitted or empty on create). Custom IDs must start with an alphanumeric character and contain only alphanumeric characters, dots, underscores, or hyphens (max 254 chars).

namespace.description: Namespace this proxy belongs to. Read-only on the wire — set from the `X-Ferrum-Namespace` request header (or the `ferrum` default) on every create/update; any value in the request body is ignored. See the API description for namespace semantics.

name.description: Optional friendly name. Must be unique across all proxies when set.

listen_path.description:
URL path prefix, `=/exact-path`, or `~regex` this proxy matches. Must start with `/` for literal prefix matching, `=/` for exact whole-path matching, or `~` for regex matching (e.g., `~^/api/v[0-9]+$`). Regex patterns are compiled at creation time and auto-anchored with `^` and `$` for full-path matching if not already present. To allow sub-path matching, end the pattern with `.*` (e.g., `~/api/v[0-9]+/.*`).

**Required for HTTP-family proxies UNLESS `hosts` is non-empty.** An HTTP proxy with neither `hosts` nor `listen_path` set is rejected — that would route every request on every host and collides with every other catch-all.

**MUST be omitted / null for stream-family proxies** (`tcp`, `tcps`, `udp`, `dtls`). Stream proxies route on `listen_port`.

When `listen_path` is null on an HTTP proxy, the proxy matches any path under the configured `hosts`. `strip_listen_path` is a no-op (nothing to strip); `backend_path` (if set) prepends to the forwarded path.

The combination of `(hosts, listen_path)` must be unique across all HTTP proxies in the same namespace.

**Must already be a canonical policy path.** Request paths are canonicalized at the frontend boundary before route lookup: percent-escapes of characters that are legal literally in a path are decoded (`/%61dmin` becomes `/admin`) and every other escape is rejected with `400`: encoded separators (`%2F`, `%3F`, `%23`), double encodings (`%25…`), encoded control characters, invalid escapes, and escapes of bytes outside that decode set (`%20`, `%7B`, and any percent-encoded non-ASCII byte). Dot segments and backslashes are rejected in both spellings — literal (`/a/../b`, `/a/./b`, `/a\b`) and encoded (`%2e%2e`, `%5C`) — because the URL parser that builds the backend request line removes dot segments and reads `\` as a separator. A segment whose text before the first `;` is `.` or `..` (`..;`, `.;x`, `%2e%2e;`, `..%3B`) is a dot segment too, because backends that strip path parameters resolve it as one. A non-final empty segment (`//`, `/a//b`) and a segment that is empty before its first `;` (`/;x/a`) are rejected too, because backends that collapse `//` would resolve a different path; a trailing slash is allowed. A `.` inside a segment (`/v1.0/users`) is an ordinary path character. A `;` on an ordinary segment (`/v1;version=2`) is refused after route lookup unless the matched proxy sets `allow_path_parameters`, so a literal `listen_path` containing `;` requires that opt-in.

A literal `listen_path` containing any of the above is unreachable, and admission rejects it on every create, update, batch, restore, and config-load path. A `~regex` `listen_path` is a pattern rather than a literal path, so only the percent-escape rules apply to it: `\` and `.` are regex syntax there, and `~^/v1\.0/.*` matching the reachable canonical path `/v1.0/x` stays valid. See `docs/request_path_canonicalization.md`.

hosts.description:
Optional list of hostnames this proxy matches. Empty means match all hosts. Supports exact hostnames (`api.example.com`) and wildcard prefixes (`*.example.com`). Entries are normalized to lowercase on admission (CRUD create/update, batch, restore, and config loaders). Must match the format `[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9.-]*[a-z0-9])?` for exact hosts or `*.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9.-]*[a-z0-9])?` for wildcards.

For HTTP-family proxies, either `hosts` or `listen_path` must be set (both may be set together). A host-only proxy (hosts set, no listen_path) matches any path under the configured hosts.

For stream-family proxies (`tcp`, `tcps`, `udp`, `dtls`), `hosts` is the TLS/DTLS `server_name` (SNI) route predicate. It is accepted only on an opaque listener that terminates nothing — `passthrough: true`, or `backend_scheme: tcp` with `frontend_tls: false` — because only such a listener can read a ClientHello. Setting it on a terminating (`frontend_tls: true`), backend-TLS-originating (`tcps`), or non-passthrough `udp`/`dtls` proxy is rejected with a field-specific 400 rather than silently ignored. Proxies sharing one `listen_port` resolve in a fixed tier order (exact host, wildcard, then the single empty-`hosts` catch-all); admission rejects a tie inside one tier, more than one catch-all, and mixed `passthrough` on a port.

backend_scheme.description:
Wire-level scheme the proxy uses to talk to its backend. Optional for HTTP-family proxies — defaults to `https` when omitted. Plaintext backends must set `backend_scheme: http`; otherwise an HTTPS dial of an HTTP origin fails with a generic 502. **Required for stream-family proxies** (`tcp`, `tcps`, `udp`, `dtls`); validation rejects stream proxies that omit it.
gRPC and WebSocket are no longer schemes — they are detected per-request from the incoming traffic (content-type, Upgrade/Connection headers, HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT). A single `https` proxy transparently serves a mix of REST, gRPC, and WebSocket traffic on the same backend pool.
HTTPS backends are classified at startup for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3 support. Plain HTTP traffic uses the native H3 backend pool automatically when the concrete target is classified as H3-capable.

**WebSocket requests arriving over HTTP/3** are supported via RFC 9220 Extended CONNECT (`:method=CONNECT`, `:protocol=websocket`). The H3 frontend bridges to an HTTP/1.1 Upgrade backend connection — the same `connect_websocket_backend()` helper the H1/H2 frontends use — so the backend sees a normal HTTP/1.1 WebSocket regardless of the frontend transport. Same plugin pipeline (`on_ws_frame`, `on_ws_disconnect`, sticky-session cookies). Gated by `FERRUM_HTTP3_WEBSOCKET_ENABLED` (default `true`); when false the H3 server does not advertise `SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL` and the bridge returns 501.

backend_host.description: Backend server hostname or IP. Required when `upstream_id` is not set. When `upstream_id` is set, this field may be omitted (empty on the wire) and is ignored — upstream targets provide the dial address.

backend_port.description: Backend server port. Required (>= 1) when `upstream_id` is not set. When `upstream_id` is set, this field may be omitted (0 on the wire) and is ignored — upstream targets provide the dial port.

backend_path.description: Optional path prefix prepended to forwarded requests

strip_listen_path.description: Strip the matched `listen_path` prefix before forwarding to the backend. No-op when `listen_path` is null (host-only proxies have no prefix to strip).

preserve_host_header.description: Forward the original Host header to the backend

allow_path_parameters.description: Accept RFC 3986 `;` path parameters (matrix parameters) in request paths routed to this proxy. With the default `false`, a request whose canonical path contains a `;` (literal or `%3B`, for example `/admin;x/users`) is refused with `400` (`path_parameter`) after route lookup and before any plugin runs, because backends such as Tomcat and Spring strip `;…` from every segment and would execute a different path than routing and policy evaluated. Enable it only for backends that use matrix parameters: routing, policy, and the backend request line then carry the `;` unchanged, so policy keyed on a parameter-free path does not match those requests. A request is still refused when its path with every parameter removed belongs to a different proxy (`/admin;x/users` on an opted-in `/` when an `/admin` proxy exists); a less specific ancestor of this proxy's own literal `listen_path` does not count, so a catch-all `/` does not shadow `/api;v=1`. Dot segments with a parameter (`..;`) and segments that are empty before their `;` (`/;x/admin`) are refused either way. A literal `listen_path` containing `;` requires `true`. HTTP-family proxies only; stream proxies must leave it `false`.

backend_read_timeout_ms.description: Backend read timeout in milliseconds (default 30000). For HTTP/gRPC proxies it bounds backend response reads and is also the total, not idle, deadline for any client request upload that Ferrum must buffer before backend dispatch. A buffered upload that exceeds the deadline is rejected with HTTP 408 or gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; streaming pass-through uploads are unaffected. For TCP proxies, this is a per-direction inactivity timeout on the backend read path. 0 disables these bounds.

backend_write_timeout_ms.description: Backend write timeout in milliseconds. For TCP proxies, this is a per-direction inactivity timeout on the backend write path. 0 = disabled.

backend_tls_client_cert_path.description: Path to mTLS client certificate (PEM). Max 4096 characters. When admin namespace-claim enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`, or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace; any other reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is loaded. A value already stored in this field is exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

backend_tls_client_key_path.description: Path to mTLS client private key (PEM), or a pkcs11 signer URI with the optional pkcs11 build feature. Module overrides require admission by FERRUM_PKCS11_MODULE_ALLOWED_PATHS on each node. Without that policy, omit module options to use FERRUM_PKCS11_MODULE_PATH. Max 4096 characters. Inline PEM key material is withheld from every non-admin read (`[REDACTED]`; a fingerprint in `GET /config/export`); references stay visible. When admin namespace-claim enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`, or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace; any other reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is loaded. A value already stored in this field is exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

backend_tls_server_ca_cert_path.description: Path (or typed source URI) for the custom CA bundle used for backend TLS verification. Max 4096 characters. The reserved value `system://` selects the built-in system/webpki trust anchors explicitly: unlike leaving this field null, it does NOT fall back to the global `FERRUM_TLS_CA_BUNDLE_PATH` and never inherits `FERRUM_TLS_NO_VERIFY`. `system://` requires `backend_tls_verify_server_cert: true` and must be spelled exactly, with no path or query options. When admin namespace-claim enforcement is on, or the token carries an `ns` claim even with enforcement off, an `operator` may set only inline PEM, `system://`, or a `k8s://` Secret in the addressed namespace; any other reference it introduces is refused with `400` before the material is loaded. A value already stored in this field is exempt, and `admin`-role tokens are not restricted.

dns_override.description:
Override backend DNS resolution with a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address.
Applies to every hostname selected for the proxy, including
load-balanced targets. A reqwest target that is itself an IP literal
must equal the override; conflicting direct targets are rejected at
admission and runtime-selected conflicts fail closed with 502.

dns_cache_ttl_seconds.description: DNS cache TTL override in seconds

plugins.description: Plugin configurations applied to this proxy. `PUT /proxies/{id}` is presence-aware for this one field: an omitted `plugins` key preserves the stored associations rather than detaching them (the `default: []` would otherwise silently remove an authentication plugin on a partial replace body). Send `"plugins": []` explicitly to clear them; any present array replaces them wholesale.

pool_idle_timeout_seconds.description: Idle connection timeout in seconds (overrides global)

pool_http2_keep_alive_interval_seconds.description: HTTP/2 PING interval in seconds (overrides global)

pool_http2_keep_alive_timeout_seconds.description: HTTP/2 PING timeout in seconds (overrides global)

pool_http2_initial_stream_window_size.description:
HTTP/2 initial per-stream flow-control window size in bytes (overrides global).
Larger values improve single-stream throughput. Range: 65535–134217728 (128 MiB). Default: 8388608 (8 MiB).
Applies while adaptive windowing is off (the default); enabling adaptive replaces this fixed size
with hyper/reqwest BDP probing that starts at 65535 bytes.
Setting this (or the connection window) without also setting pool_http2_adaptive_window
explicitly auto-disables adaptive at this proxy so the fixed window takes effect.

pool_http2_initial_connection_window_siz.description:
HTTP/2 initial connection-level flow-control window size in bytes (overrides global).
Aggregate budget shared across all concurrent streams. Range: 65535–134217728 (128 MiB). Default: 33554432 (32 MiB).
Same adaptive-vs-fixed precedence as pool_http2_initial_stream_window_size.

pool_http2_adaptive_window.description:
Enable adaptive flow-control (BDP probing) for HTTP/2 connections (overrides global).
Default: false — the fixed initial stream/connection windows apply. While enabled, adaptive
windowing replaces those fixed sizes: hyper restarts both at 65535 bytes and grows the connection
window only as the link is measured, which fragments hundreds of concurrent streams into tiny
DATA frames and can trip h2's small-frame flood budget (GOAWAY ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM). Its BDP
PING/SETTINGS traffic can also deadlock a connection carrying large bodies in both directions,
especially when both peers enable adaptive windowing; h2 stops reading while a control-frame
write waits for socket capacity (issue #6073, upstream https://github.com/hyperium/h2/issues/975).
This describes hyper/reqwest HTTP/2 connections; HBONE uses a separate raw-h2 window policy
and does not enable this BDP PING/SETTINGS behavior.
An explicit adaptive choice remains authoritative even alongside window overrides; omit this
field when setting explicit windows to auto-disable adaptive so fixed sizes apply.

pool_http2_max_frame_size.description:
Maximum HTTP/2 frame payload size in bytes (overrides global).
Range: 16384–1048576 (1 MiB). Default: 1048576 (1 MiB).

pool_http2_max_concurrent_streams.description:
Maximum concurrent HTTP/2 streams per backend connection (overrides global).
Range: 1–2147483647. Default: 1000.

pool_http3_connections_per_backend.description:
Number of QUIC connections per HTTP/3 backend (overrides global
FERRUM_HTTP3_CONNECTIONS_PER_BACKEND). Multiple connections distribute
QUIC frame processing across driver tasks. Range: 1–256. Default: 4.

upstream_id.description:
Reference to an existing Upstream for load-balanced backends. When set,
`backend_host` and `backend_port` may be omitted; the selected
upstream target supplies the dial address. The referenced upstream
must exist at creation time. Deleting an upstream that is referenced
by a proxy is blocked.

upstream_subset.description:
Named subset within `upstream_id` to route to. The subset must be
defined in the referenced upstream's `subsets` list; invalid subset
references are rejected during config/admin validation. Matching is
exact: a target belongs to a subset when its `tags` contain every
label in the subset selector with the same value.

listen_port.description:
Listen-port identity for this proxy (must be >= 1 when set).

Stream family (`tcp`/`tcps`/`udp`/`dtls`): required. The proxy binds
this port and routes by it (not by path). A stream proxy normally binds
its own dedicated port; proxies may share one port only by forming a
single shared listener — an opaque-TLS SNI group (all `passthrough:
true`, or all opaque `tcp` listeners with at least one declaring
`hosts`) or an L4 `stream_match` group. Any other duplicate port is
rejected. In database mode, the Admin API also rejects ports that
conflict with gateway reserved ports (proxy/admin/gRPC listeners) or
are already bound on the host. In CP mode, local port checks are
skipped since stream proxies run on remote DP nodes.

HTTP family: optional. When set, the proxy is port-scoped and only
matches requests accepted on that frontend port (or the protocol-class
remap when a single HTTP/HTTPS Gateway listener port is projected onto
`FERRUM_PROXY_HTTP_PORT` / `FERRUM_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT`). When omitted,
the proxy remains port-agnostic and matches any HTTP-family frontend
(manual / non-Kubernetes default). Distinct `listen_port` values do not
conflict on the same `hosts`+`listen_path`. A `listen_port` equal to
`FERRUM_PROXY_HTTP_PORT` or `FERRUM_PROXY_HTTPS_PORT` must match that
frontend's class (`http_tls_listen_ports`) and carry no dedicated
Sidecar ingress bind; in database mode the Admin API rejects either
conflict with `409`. CP mode skips this check.

frontend_tls.description:
Terminate encryption on the gateway side for incoming connections.
For TCP: uses the gateway's TLS certificate.
For UDP: uses DTLS with ECDSA P-256 or Ed25519 certificates
(configured via FERRUM_DTLS_CERT_PATH/FERRUM_DTLS_KEY_PATH env vars).

passthrough.description:
Forward encrypted client bytes directly to the backend without
terminating TLS (TCP) or DTLS (UDP). The proxy peeks at the
ClientHello to extract SNI for logging but does not decrypt traffic.
Only valid for stream proxies (tcp, tcps, udp, dtls).
Mutually exclusive with frontend_tls.

SNI-based routing is not exclusive to this flag: an ordinary
`backend_scheme: tcp` listener with `frontend_tls: false` is equally
opaque and routes by `hosts` on the same plane. Every candidate
sharing one `listen_port` must agree on `passthrough`, because the
shared listener socket is built from one representative before any
route is selected.

tcp_idle_timeout_seconds.description:
TCP stream idle timeout in seconds. After this duration of no data transfer
in either direction, the connection is closed. When omitted, uses the global
FERRUM_TCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default: 300s / 5 min). Set to 0 to disable.
Only applicable for tcp/tcps schemes.

stream_proxy_protocol.description:
Enable inbound PROXY protocol on this stream proxy listener. The framing
depends on the scheme:

* tcp / tcps: PROXY protocol v1 text or v2 binary (auto-detected), read once
  at the head of each accepted connection. A connection that does not begin with
  a valid header is closed immediately (fail closed).
* udp / dtls: the PROXY protocol v2 DGRAM envelope, present on EVERY datagram
  (a session-scoped header cannot be trusted on an unordered, lossy transport).
  A datagram that does not decode is dropped; nothing is forwarded and no
  session is created. When FERRUM_DATAGRAM_PROXY_PROTOCOL_SECRET is set, the
  HMAC-SHA-256 tag is computed over a versioned domain-separation prefix
  naming the exact receiving listener (receive-boundary protocol, canonical
  bind address, port), so an envelope minted for listener A can never
  authenticate on listener B under one process-global root secret — for every
  command and family, LOCAL and AF_UNSPEC included. The envelope's declared
  destination port is compared to this proxy's listen_port as defense in
  depth. Each authenticated envelope also carries an authenticated freshness
  record (sender id, epoch, monotonic sequence, timestamp), and the receiver
  keeps a bounded per-sender sliding replay window, so a duplicate or stale
  datagram is dropped before any session, plugin, or backend work. LOCAL and
  AF_UNSPEC still never set a forwarded identity. Ferrum never emits the
  envelope toward the backend, and replies are sent back to the socket peer
  unwrapped.

Trust requirement: the forwarded address is honoured only when the socket peer
(the load balancer's own IP) belongs to the FERRUM_TRUSTED_PROXIES CIDR set. A
connection from an untrusted peer on a PROXY-protocol-enabled listener is also
closed (TCP) or dropped (UDP/DTLS) to prevent direct-connect clients from
spoofing their source IP. On udp / dtls, set
FERRUM_DATAGRAM_PROXY_PROTOCOL_SECRET to additionally require an HMAC-SHA-256
tag and a freshness record on every datagram; source addresses are spoofable on
UDP, so that secret is what makes datagram metadata trustworthy off a protected
path. Without it the listener stays in the address-trust posture, which has
neither cryptographic authenticity nor freshness.

After a trusted parse, client_ip in the stream context (and in stream logs and
authz plugins) is the forwarded source IP; direct_client_ip retains the raw
socket peer (the LB's own IP). This mirrors XFF + FERRUM_TRUSTED_PROXIES
on the HTTP path.

Only valid for tcp / tcps / udp / dtls stream proxies. Setting it on an
HTTP-family proxy produces a validation error: HTTP-family proxies share the
global HTTP/HTTPS listeners, which enable inbound PROXY protocol listener-wide
with the FERRUM_FRONTEND_PROXY_PROTOCOL_HTTP / FERRUM_FRONTEND_PROXY_PROTOCOL_HTTPS
environment settings instead.

Default: null / false (disabled; socket peer is always used as client_ip).

backend_proxy_protocol.description:
Opt-in outbound PROXY protocol written on backend TCP connects for this
stream proxy. When set to `v2`, Ferrum prepends a PROXY protocol v2 binary
header carrying the trusted stream client_ip (and port) immediately after
the backend TCP connect — before any relayed application bytes, and before
the backend TLS handshake when originating TLS. Compatible with passthrough
(the header precedes the client's encrypted ClientHello on the wire).

Source addresses honor the inbound PROXY trust decision: when
stream_proxy_protocol is enabled and the peer is trusted, the forwarded
client identity is advertised; otherwise the accept-time socket peer is used.

Only valid for tcp / tcps stream proxies. Setting it on UDP, DTLS, or HTTP
proxies produces a validation error (PROXY protocol is TCP-borne). UDP
outbound PROXY is intentionally out of scope.

Default: null (disabled — backends see the gateway egress IP).

stream_match.description:
Optional bounded L4 connection matcher for TCP/TCP+TLS proxies.
Predicates within one arm are ANDed; arms are ORed in declaration
order. Any predicate whose trusted connection evidence is absent
denies that arm. Source IP is the canonical authoritative client IP
after trusted PROXY-protocol processing, never an untrusted
application header.
Destination IP comes from trusted original-destination capture.
Gateway identity is trusted listener configuration only.

Omitted, null, `{}`, or `{ "arms": [] }` means no additional matcher.
A non-empty arm must contain at least one predicate. Invalid or
uncompiled configured matchers fail closed. Only valid for TCP-borne
stream proxies; UDP and DTLS configurations are rejected.

websocket_idle_timeout_seconds.description:
WebSocket relay idle timeout in seconds for upgraded sessions on this proxy
(HTTP-family proxies; applies to H1/H2/H3 frontends and both the frame-parsed
and tunnel-mode relays). The session closes only when neither direction
produces activity (frames, including Ping/Pong, or transport bytes) within the
window; activity from either side keeps it open. When omitted, uses the global
FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default: 300s / 5 min). Set to 0 to
disable only the idle bound for this proxy; the finite global WebSocket
maximum lifetime still applies. Maximum 86400 (24h).
HTTP/3 caveat: on QUIC frontends the transport idle timeout
FERRUM_HTTP3_IDLE_TIMEOUT (default 30s) also applies. On an
otherwise-idle H3 connection, QUIC may close before a longer WebSocket
idle timer; multiplexed H3 connections with other active streams may
stay open. Startup/reload warnings are logged only for affected proxies
when an H3 WebSocket listener is actually reachable.

websocket_permessage_deflate.description:
RFC 7692 `permessage-deflate` handling for WebSocket upgrades on this
proxy (HTTP-family proxies only; stream proxies must use `strip`).

- `strip` (default): the client's `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions` offer
  never reaches the backend and no extension is negotiated, so every
  message stays inspectable by WebSocket frame plugins.
- `passthrough`: `permessage-deflate` offer elements reach the backend
  unchanged and the backend's `permessage-deflate` answer reaches the
  client unchanged on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT, and HTTP/3
  Extended CONNECT. Every other extension token is still stripped. A
  session that negotiates the extension is relayed as raw bytes, so
  gateway WebSocket frame and fragment limits do not apply to it.
  Refused (400) on a proxy with any plugin that requires the parsed
  WebSocket relay (`waf`, `ws_frame_logging`,
  `ws_message_size_limiting`, `ws_rate_limiting`, an `api_chargeback`
  that prices bandwidth, or a custom plugin whose
  `requires_websocket_framing()` is true), whether attached
  directly, through a proxy group, or inherited from a global plugin.
- `terminate`: the gateway negotiates `permessage-deflate` with the
  client and with the backend independently (the backend receives
  the gateway's own `permessage-deflate` offer), inflates every
  message before the frame relay and its plugins see it, and
  re-deflates toward each leg that negotiated compression. Every
  plugin stays allowed and sees plaintext. Decompression is bounded:
  a compressed frame may not exceed the frame ceiling, a frame may not
  inflate past it, and a message may not inflate past
  `FERRUM_WEBSOCKET_PERMESSAGE_DEFLATE_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` (default
  1 MiB; `0` opts into the reassembled-message ceiling); exceeding
  either closes with 1009. An invalid backend answer (including a
  foreign extension, a malformed list, or a non-ASCII value) refuses
  the upgrade with 502.
  Applies on HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 Extended CONNECT, and HTTP/3 Extended
  CONNECT.

udp_idle_timeout_seconds.description:
UDP session idle timeout in seconds. After this duration of inactivity,
the UDP session mapping is removed. Only applicable for udp/dtls protocols.

udp_max_response_amplification_factor.description:
Maximum allowed response amplification factor for UDP proxies.
Backend→client datagrams share one remaining payload-byte budget
per admitted client request (`payload_size * factor`, cumulative
across replies). A zero-length request receives an explicit
one-byte reply allowance so it cannot black-hole the session;
nonempty requests retain the exact configured payload ratio. Every
backend response datagram consumes at least one unit of remaining
budget, so a zero-length reply cannot bypass a finite factor. This
protects against UDP amplification attacks (e.g., spoofed-source
reflection). Finite values must be greater than 0 and at most 1024.

**Omitting the field is not unlimited.** Every `udp` / `dtls` proxy
that leaves it unset is normalized to the finite default `8.0`,
whatever the configuration source (file, database, admin API,
CP→DP, mesh, Gateway API), so a UDP proxy is never an open
reflector by default. `0` is the explicit operator opt-out meaning
"no limit"; it is accepted only on `udp` / `dtls` proxies and the
affected listener logs a warning at startup. Gateway API `UDPRoute`
translation projects the same `8.0` default unless a Ferrum
`UDPResponseAmplificationPolicy` supplies a finite override or an
explicit dual-acknowledged unlimited mode, which is materialized as
`0`. Only applicable for `udp` / `dtls` proxies.

allowed_methods.description:
Optional list of HTTP methods this proxy accepts. When null (default),
all methods are allowed. When set, requests with methods not in the list
receive 405 Method Not Allowed before any plugin processing.

allowed_ws_origins.description:
Optional list of allowed WebSocket Origin values (e.g., ["https://example.com"]).
When non-empty, WebSocket upgrade requests must include an Origin header matching
one of these values (case-insensitive comparison).
Empty array (default) allows all origins. Entries are literal origins of the
form `scheme://host[:port]`; `*` is not a wildcard and is rejected at Admin API
create/update (POST/PUT/PATCH proxies, batch, restore), file-mode loads, and
`ferrum-edge validate`. Existing database/CP rows containing `*` still load,
with a warning naming the proxy. Protects against Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH).

Independent of the `cors` plugin, which does not run on WebSocket upgrades.
Operators with a strict CORS allowlist on the same proxy should mirror those
origins here. See docs/routing.md#websocket-origin-admission.

WebSocket over HTTP/1.1 (`Upgrade: websocket`), HTTP/2
(RFC 8441 Extended CONNECT), and HTTP/3 (RFC 9220 Extended
CONNECT) are all supported and use the same Origin check.
The H3 path is gated by `FERRUM_HTTP3_WEBSOCKET_ENABLED`
(default `true`); see `docs/http3.md` for the H3-specific
bridge architecture.

response_body_mode.description:
Response body handling mode.

- `stream` (default): Passes response bytes through as they arrive for
  lower latency and memory usage. If any plugin attached to this proxy
  requires response body buffering (e.g., response_transformer), the
  gateway automatically buffers regardless of this setting.
- `buffer`: Always buffers the full response body before running
  after-proxy plugins, even if no plugin requires it. Use this when you
  need to guarantee the complete body is available for inspection.

api_spec_id.description:
ID of the `ApiSpec` that created this proxy via the spec-import admin
API (`POST /api-specs`). `null` for proxies created via direct admin
endpoints (`POST /proxies`). When set, the proxy participates in
spec-level ownership: `PUT /api-specs/{id}` replaces this proxy as part
of the bundle, and `DELETE /api-specs/{id}` deletes this proxy (and
its plugins via FK cascade).

ProxyCreate.description:
Request body for creating or updating a proxy. Same schema as Proxy
but `id`, `created_at`, and `updated_at` are optional (server-managed).

**Validation rules** (enforced at admin API + file/DB load time):
- HTTP-family proxies: at least one of `hosts` or `listen_path` must
  be set. A proxy with neither is rejected (400). Optional `listen_port`
  scopes the route to that frontend port (or the HTTP/HTTPS protocol
  remap); omit it for port-agnostic matching.
- Stream-family proxies (`tcp`/`tcps`/`udp`/`dtls`): `listen_path`
  MUST be null/omitted, and `listen_port` MUST be set,
  and `backend_scheme` MUST be set explicitly.
- HTTP-family `backend_scheme` defaults to `https` when omitted.
  Plaintext backends must set `backend_scheme: http`.
- Unknown fields are rejected. Backend H3 selection is runtime
  capability-driven for `Https` backends — there is no scheme for it.
- `backend_host` and `backend_port` may be omitted when `upstream_id`
  is set. They remain required for a direct-backend proxy.

ResourceLabels.description: Informational operator metadata. Keys must be nonblank; keys and values cannot contain control characters. Runtime length limits are UTF-8 bytes (128 per key, 512 per value). Independent of target tags, routing, access control and api_spec_id. Omitted labels on resource PUT preserve the current map; an explicit map replaces it and {} clears it. Labels are retained in GET/list, backup/restore, file configuration and CP/DP sync. The provisioned-by label identifies the application that provisioned a resource; it is caller-supplied information, not proof of ownership. Resource labels landed on main in pull request 5483 on 2026-09-12, and every published release through v0.9.4 rejects the `labels` field with unknown field `labels`. v0.9.5 is the first tagged release with resource labels; operators and clients should use v0.9.5 or later.

retryable_status_codes.description: HTTP status codes eligible for retry. Empty by default: no status-code retries occur unless codes are listed.

retryable_methods.description: HTTP methods eligible for retry. Must be valid HTTP methods.

retry_on_connect_failure.description:
Retry on TCP-level failures (connect refused, DNS failure, TLS
error, timeout) independently of `retryable_status_codes`.

source_labels.description:
Kubernetes label key/value pairs that must all match trustworthy
workload identity evidence. Empty label values are valid. Missing,
ambiguous, or unauthenticated label evidence denies the arm.

source_namespace.description:
Exact Kubernetes source namespace from authenticated SPIFFE/workload
identity. Missing authenticated namespace evidence denies the arm.

source_subnets.description:
IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs or individual IP addresses. Entries are parsed
strictly at admission. The authoritative canonical client IP after
the trusted PROXY boundary must belong to at least one entry.

destination_subnets.description:
IPv4/IPv6 CIDRs or individual IP addresses, parsed strictly at
admission. The trusted captured original destination must belong to
at least one entry; missing capture evidence denies the arm.

gateways.description:
Exact trusted gateway bindings: `mesh` or canonical
`namespace/name`. Short names are rejected outside translation
because no namespace can be inferred safely. Missing listener
binding denies the arm; the value is never wire-derived.

arms.description:
OR-ordered match arms. Declaration order is semantic both within
this list and across proxies sharing a stream listener; an earlier
unconstrained candidate shadows later candidates. Empty means no
additional L4 matcher.
